```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(repair)
```

A measurement model can include person-level random intercepts/slopes and
additional random effects for occasions within each person. REPAIR can target
the person coefficients while incorporating these **nuisance effects** into
their scoring-error covariance. This extension currently applies to Gaussian
`lme4::lmer()` fits.

## Fit a person and day model

The bundled reference contains synthetic data for 48 people, each with multiple
days and repeated observations within each day. Practice is a simulated
person-level predictor. Day numbers are local to each person. These are
implementation reference datasets, not real participant data or the paper's
published simulation results.

```{r measurement}
reference <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "nested-workflow-reference.rds", package = "repair"))
example <- reference$cases$nested_intercept
head(example$data[c("person", "day", "x", "y")])
head(example$people)

growth <- lme4::lmer(
  y ~ x + offset(off) + (1 + x | person) + (1 | person:day),
  data = example$data, weights = prior, na.action = na.exclude,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000))
)
models <- list(growth = growth)
repair_effects(models)
```

`person` is the target grouping factor; `person:day` is a nuisance grouping factor.
The fitted model's weights, offsets, fixed effects, and effective observations
are retained. Check measurement-model adequacy and optimizer messages with the
usual lme4 tools before structural analysis.

## Select one target group per model

Both groups have an `(Intercept)`, so a model name alone cannot identify the
person intercept. Use `group = "person"` in `re()`. Names must match the
`repair_effects()` catalog; the person table's ID column can have a different name.
A unique term can still be selected without a group qualifier.

```{r fit}
equation <- re("x", model = "growth", group = "person") ~
  re("(Intercept)", model = "growth", group = "person") + practice
analysis <- repair_data(equation, models, example$people, id = "person")
head(repair_scores(analysis))
head(repair_score_covariance(analysis))

fit <- repair(equation, models, example$people, id = "person")
repair_coefficients(fit)
summary(fit)$measurement_models$growth
```

This regresses the latent person slope deviation on the person intercept
deviation and practice. Scores remain deviations from fitted fixed effects.
The selected intercept/slope scoring-error covariance is retained. Nuisance
coefficients do not become structural predictors or outcomes: all references to
one measurement model must select the same target group.

Reported effect labels include the group for models with multiple groups. The
stable tables retain their existing schemas and explicit model/group/term/ID
keys. The structural summary identifies the verified nuisance groups; their
names are also in `summary(fit)$measurement_models$growth$nuisance_groups`.

## What enters scoring and reliability?

For person j, the target-specific covariance is

\[
R_{T,j} = R_{e,j} + \sum_{g\ne T} Z_{g,j}G_gZ_{g,j}^{\mathsf T}.
\]

Ordinary residual covariance includes the fitted residual scale and prior
weights. The nuisance contributions include all day effects for that person.
Person random effects are excluded from this covariance because they are the
target signal. GLS supplies a joint score and error covariance
`(Z_T' R_T^-1 Z_T)^-1`. Adding only a day variance to the diagonal would lose the
covariance between observations sharing a day.

Posterior reliability uses the same `R_T`, with the fitted target prior
covariance G added for the posterior calculation. Ignoring nuisance variance in
reliability would overstate available information.

```{r reliability}
repair_reliability(fit)[, c("term", "measure", "reliability", "n_people")]
repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "cohort")
repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "measurement")
```

The fitted lmer model supplies mutually independent random-effect blocks and
independent ordinary residuals, conditional on fitted parameters. The structural
SEs remain conditional on those fitted quantities; they do not propagate
measurement-parameter estimation uncertainty or provide bootstrap inference.
The original diagnostics, omission policy, and normal-interval interpretation
continue to apply.

## More than one nuisance group, including slopes

Every nuisance group must satisfy the same containment rule. For example, both
day and block can be contained within people even if day and block cross within
a person. Nuisance coefficients within a block can be correlated.

```{r multiple-nuisance}
complex <- reference$cases$nested_slope
growth2 <- lme4::lmer(
  y ~ x + offset(off) + (1 + x | person) +
    (1 + within | person:day) + (1 | person:block),
  data = complex$data, weights = prior, na.action = na.exclude,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 100000))
)
fit2 <- repair(equation, list(growth = growth2), complex$people, "person")
repair_coefficients(fit2)
```

Separate random-effect blocks for the target, such as `(x || person)`, are also
supported. Several measurement models can each have eligible nuisance groups;
combining them still requires the explicit cross-model error policy in
`vignette("multiple-models")`.

## Shared effects remain rejected

Containment is verified from **all effective fitted observations**: each nuisance
level must occur in exactly one target person. This is a membership check, not a
check of whether a name contains a colon. Globally unique visit IDs can qualify
without a colon. The check precedes structural cohort selection, so omission or
requesting just one person per school cannot bypass it. An estimated zero
nuisance variance does not waive the membership rule.

`(1 | day)` means a shared day effect if the same day number occurs for several
people. `(1 | person:day)` represents distinct effects for each person's days.
Choose the grouping specification from the scientific design: do not split a
truly shared school, item, or calendar-day effect merely to pass validation.

If people j and k share a nuisance effect, their scoring errors can have
nonzero cross-person covariance. The current structural estimator accepts
within-person blocks and cannot account for that dependence. Shared nuisance
levels therefore produce an explicit error, even with `na_action = "omit"`.
Targeting days while treating their shared person effect as nuisance also fails
this rule. Lower-level scoring of shared structures remains experimental and
is not an alternative route to validated structural inference.

Multilevel nlme fits remain unsupported. For current model and inference limits,
see `vignette("support-and-troubleshooting")`.

## Validation and reproducibility

The tests refit both models from observations and compare scores, complete
within-person covariance, posterior reliability, structural estimates, SEs,
coefficient covariance, and normal intervals with independent frozen references.
Both R and C++ estimation backends are checked. Reference GLS/posterior matrices
are calculated directly from fitted measurement quantities without loading
repair; the structural estimates are cross-checked against the companion
production estimator and algebra audit. The generator and source provenance are
in `dev/generate_nested_fixtures.R` and the bundled reference's `provenance`.
These comparisons establish per-dataset implementation agreement, not nominal
coverage across all nested designs.
